topic.focus: optimal lookback window length for cross-sectional price momentum
topic.angle: formation period 6-12-18 months, skip 1 month, US equities 2020-2025

papers.title: All Days Are Not Created Equal: Understanding Momentum by Learning to Weight Past Returns
papers.hypothesis: Replace uniform 12-month lookback with a learned sparse weighting over the prior 231 trading days, over-weighting days coinciding with earnings announcements, market-wide jumps, and large individual-stock return realizations.
papers.rationale: Published Journal of Banking & Finance 2025; the optimal sparse weight vector concentrates ~30% of weight on just 2 of 231 days, beating standard 12-1 and surviving post-2010. Directly actionable: compute a weighted-rank signal where returns on earnings dates and market-jump days count more. This is novel relative to any uniform-window ranking and could materially boost the champion's signal quality with a targeted implementation.

papers.title: Evaluating a 12-1 Month Momentum Strategy (2005–2024): Momentum in Large-Cap Equities
papers.hypothesis: Long-short 12-1 momentum on large-cap US equities produces a negative net Sharpe after 2005; however, the long-only top-decile leg remains viable at +7.9% annualized, suggesting the signal is intact but the short leg destroys value during crash rebounds.
papers.rationale: Posted SSRN February 2026; uses survivorship-bias-free S&P 500 history 2006-2024. Negative result for the full strategy is informative: it confirms the 12-1 lookback is sound on the long side but losers should not be shorted. For a long-only walk-forward system this is a positive confirmation. The cost model (10 bps/side) and gap-aware return construction are methodologically rigorous comparables.

papers.title: Empirical Determinants of Momentum: A Perspective Using International Data
papers.hypothesis: A 9-month formation / 3-month holding period (with 1-month skip) outperforms the canonical 12-1-1 construction and is explained by slow diffusion of information ('frog in the pan'), suggesting trimming the formation window to ~189 days and extending the hold to 63 days.
papers.rationale: Goyal, Jegadeesh & Subrahmanyam in Review of Finance Vol 29 Jan 2025; tests a range of (J, K) combinations internationally and finds 9/3 optimal. The frog-in-the-pan mechanism (small incremental news underreacted to) is distinct from pure price continuation and implies that a 252-day window over-weights old stale signal. Trimming to 189 days is a concrete, low-risk parameter change to test against the current champion.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Factor Momentum: Evidence from Multiple Formation Periods
papers.hypothesis: Combining a short-horizon (1–3 month) and intermediate-horizon (6–12 month) momentum signal into a composite rank captures distinct and non-spanning information, improving performance over any single formation window.
papers.rationale: Applied Economics Letters 2025; shows the short-term (1-3 month) and intermediate (6-12 month) formation windows capture different return predictability and that neither spans the other. Directly actionable as a composite rank signal: average or blend the 63-day and 252-day lookback ranks before sorting. The 'recent-past' component persists post-publication, reducing data-mining concern.

papers.title: Explaining and Predicting Momentum Performance Shifts Across Time and Sectors
papers.hypothesis: Momentum performance is predictable from sector and macro-cycle features; conditioning the 12-1 lookback strategy on a predicted-performance regime signal (trained OOS on 2018–2023) can meaningfully reduce drawdowns.
papers.rationale: Journal of Forecasting 2025 (Mamais); trained 1980–2017, tested 2018–2023 with holdout through 2024. Demonstrates that momentum crashes are partly predictable using available macro/sector inputs, not purely ex-post. Actionable as a position-sizing or universe-filter overlay: reduce exposure when the regime model flags an adverse environment, preserving the 12-1 signal structure while improving tail risk.
